incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired PD-2025-6789 — p99 latency spike for /v1/generate in eu-west cluster. Current p99: 3.2s (SLO 1.2s). Alerting rule: latency_p99_route > 2.5s for 5m.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-2025-6789 created. Assigned: @Alice H (oncall). Escalation policy: eng-oncall -> eng-sre -> eng-pltf.

Alice H: acked and on it. pulling graphs now.

Bob S: seeing a simultaneous small error increase on sidecar timeouts? Not full 5xx flood but more timeouts from sidecar -> runtime.

Carla M: traffic shift or model change recently? I can check model rollouts.

Dave Eng: nothing deployed to hosted in last 30m from deploy bot. Last deploy was 40m ago: release/2025-05-08. No canary changes.

Alice H: good—let's validate if it's traffic or runtime degradation. Dave, can you paste hotpath logs and a perf profile?

Dave Eng: pastes logs:
```
[2025-05-08T12:03:42Z] route=/v1/generate req_id=abc123 lat_ms=3200 backend=sidecar-12 kv_hit=false
[2025-05-08T12:03:43Z] route=/v1/generate req_id=def456 lat_ms=3100 backend=sidecar-14 kv_hit=false
[2025-05-08T12:03:44Z] route=/v1/embeddings req_id=ghi789 lat_ms=120 ms backend=sidecar-5 kv_hit=true
```
Looks like /v1/generate specifically hitting sidecars with unexpected tail.

infra-autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: eu-west pool CPU 78% -> 79%, GPU util 92% for serving group r-gen; scaling blocked by quota. No additional nodes available.

Alice H: ok autoscaler is at capacity. That lines up with p99 tail. Could be local KV cache eviction or hotkey. Any hotkeys for generate?

Carla M: running quick hotkey check on keys distribution...

Carla M: found a small hotkey cluster — a test client issuing many long-seq requests to /v1/generate around 11:58-12:05 UTC. Not huge qps but many long seqs causing KV cache pressure and GPU memory churn.

Sally Support: customer reports: "slow responses on autocomplete" from EU customers starting ~12:00 UTC. A few support tickets created (SUP-3321, SUP-3322).

Bob S: mitigation plan suggestions: 1) enable traffic routing fallback to lower-latency model variant (quantized q8) for eu-west; 2) temporarily throttle long-seq test client via WAF rate-limit; 3) increase KV cache retention or pin hot keys.

Alice H: prioritize quick mitigations that don't require infra quota. Option 1 and 2 look fastest. Carla, can we identify the client IP range to block or rate limit?

Carla M: giving IPs: 35.214.88.0/24 and 35.214.90.7. Looks like internal QA cluster.

Dave Eng: I can flip routing policy for eu-west on the router: route /v1/generate -> model-variant-q8-fallback for 10% -> 100% gradual shift. Command:
```
curl -XPOST "https://console.redwood/api/v1/route-update" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OPS" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","region":"eu-west","policy":{"fallback":"model-variant-q8","rollout_pct":10}}'
```
Do we want to do this now?

Alice H: yes do it. Start 10% now and monitor p99. Also Bob, please apply a temporary WAF rule to 35.214.88.0/24 to rate-limit to 5r/s.

Bob S: applying WAF rule now.

infra-autoscaler-bot: WAF rule applied: id=waf-3442, scope=eu-west, limit=5r/s for 35.214.88.0/24.

Dave Eng: route update applied, rollout 10% -> checking metrics.

(1 minute passes)

Alice H: p99 dropped to 2.1s, p95 stable. Good signal. Continue gradual. Increase rollout to 50%.

Dave Eng: bumping rollout to 50%.

(another minute)

Alice H: p99 now 1.4s, still above SLO but trending. WAF limited test client, some reduction in long-seq tail.

Carla M: KV miss rate decreased by 30% in eu-west sidecars. That matches cache pressure hypothesis.

Sally Support: Customer impact update: most EU customers reporting transient slowness; two enterprise customers flagged potential regret for SLA hit. Logged with CS.

Alice H: escalate to eng-pltf if we need a permanent capacity bump. For now keep on fallback model and maintain WAF. Start a PD bridge if PD auto-rule thinks this will persist >30m.

pagerduty-bot: PD note: incident open threshold 30m; currently 12m elapsed. No bridge created.

Bob S: I'll keep WAF in place and monitor. If p99 is back within 1.2s for 10m, we can start rolling back fallback.

Dave Eng: monitoring for any regressions from quantized variant. Early checks show token quality within thresholds on our quick evals.

Alice H: good. I'm going to hand off to Bob for continuous watch and to coordinate with platform on capacity. I'm heading out for a scheduled break — @Bob S you own until 13:00 UTC.

Bob S: ack taking over. I'll keep updates every 10m or sooner for any regression.

Sally Support: I'll send a short customer comms note to affected enterprise contacts: "We identified a latency regression in eu-west and applied traffic routing to a fallback model and temporary rate-limits; service impact mitigated and we're monitoring. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

Alice H: adding postmortem owners: Alice H (incident), Dave Eng (mitigation), Carla M (root-cause), Bob S (follow-up ops), Sally Support (customer comms).

(30 minutes later)

Bob S: p99 stable at 1.1s for past 12m. WAF still in place. Autoscaler request submitted to infra team for capacity increase — ticket INFRA-8891.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-2025-6789 resolved by user Bob S.

incident-bot: Incident closed. Please file postmortem and link any configs changed: route-update id=ru-7702, waf id=waf-3442.

Bob S: filing minimal timeline in #postmortems and will expand with root cause and follow-up actions.

Sally Support: sending customer follow-up now.

Alice H: thanks team — nice quick mitigation and ops. We'll have the longer RCA in the postmortem.
